title: Dsci-proj: normalize a backlog before asking what comes next
audience: Engineering and product teams that need explainable prioritization across changing source systems.
promise: Make the decision contract visible: different backlog shapes can describe the same decision inputs, while criteria and final judgment remain user-owned.
story: A research-issue backlog and a product backlog arrive with different field names, states, and evidence shapes.
The DS-0 contract names one canonical item model, five editable criteria, missing-input policy, and factor-level explanation requirements.
The synthetic appendix shows how each source maps into that model before any score or queue is treated as a product result.
A scenario comparison is specified as deterministic over the same normalized inputs, so a changed weight can be inspected rather than guessed.
DS-1 adapter implementation and current scenario proof remain open; the local packet is a target, not a generalized running engine.
verified_locally: DS-0 is a versioned decision contract with user-editable weights, fail-closed missing-input policy, source evidence, and deterministic scenario requirements.
The synthetic fixture contains two meaningfully different backlog shapes and three fail-closed negative cases.
The local candidate page keeps the normalized item model and the DS-1 implementation boundary visible.
The local packet includes a candidate no-auth source page, short copy, claim ledger, and reviewed 1600x900 binary.
open_gates: Implement DS-1 adapters for both backlog schemas without source-specific decision-engine changes.
Prove a real scenario comparison, explanation, and export/handoff against current product behavior.
Capture current runnable and direct-surface evidence before calling the case an implemented product.
Verify a hosted no-auth case URL and read back each external destination before release.
claim_boundary: This packet proves the DS-0 decision contract, a synthetic two-source mapping appendix, and local candidate materials. It does not claim generalized adapters, a live ranking, scenario results, hosted behavior, or publication.
